newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Broaddus - US hunger for foreign cash a worry.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Broaddus - US hunger for foreign cash a worry.

text.p: Richmond Federal Reserve Bank President Alfred Broaddus voiced some concern on Tuesday that so much of U.S. economic growth and investment in recent years has been financed with capital from abroad.

But he brushed aside worries that the United States might suffer a rapid outflow of foreign capital in the short term, saying that the stability of the U.S. economy and its financial markets act as a magnet for money from abroad.
"We need to be concerned ... that so much of our growth and investment in recent years has in fact been financed by savings overseas," Broaddus told the Association of Busness Economists.
While "that's not necessarily a bad thing," the United States needs to supplement the foreign finance with additional domestic savings, Broaddus said.
Broaddus also played down worries that the recent rise in the minimum wage would trigger a jump in inflation, although he made clear that he was opposed to the increase.
"The particular change in the minimum wage that has just been legislated is small enough that its impact on overall wage behaviour and inflation is likely to be relatively small," he said.
The minimum wage was increased on October 1 to $4.75 per hour from $4.25. It is scheduled to go up another 40 cents per hour on September 1, 1997.
